defect: Native core-report regeneration awaited subprocess creation/communicate without cancellation ownership. Runner shutdown cancelled the background report task, which could finish while its exact child remained alive. The runner then committed stopped and acknowledged local stop before the child finished writing. The complete isolated native supervisor reproduced final_publication_children=[[null]], premature_report_owner_done=true and an already acknowledged stopped SQL row while the held actual report child was live. This is not an established historical financial/no-buy cause.
repair: Admit the report coroutine once through await_owned_task and retain it through repeated parent cancellation, including subprocess creation. The actual report coroutine retains the concrete process and waits for it even after a pipe failure. Original command, working directory, priority, output decoding, failure result and report-summary behavior remain. A pre-cancelled owner admits no new task, failed admission closes the unsubmitted coroutine and internal worker cancellation is not a normal caller stop. Existing thread ownership and every trading/provider/model/activation/sizing/exit policy remain unchanged. No child is killed or restarted by this repair; it must settle before native shutdown acknowledgement.
